summary:
I followed the planner's steps. Nothing was compiled or run. Early on I made one shell call by mistake; the harness refused it and nothing ran. After that I only read and edited files.

clipboard.rs (new file, `mod clipboard;` is after `mod cli;`): `Clipboard { write: Sink }` with `system()` and `copy()`. `system()` pipes the text into `pbcopy` with stdout and stderr sent to null. `piped` always calls wait(), then returns any error from feeding the text, then checks with `ensure!` that the program exited successfully. `feed` puts contexts on its errors: "no input to write the text to" and "the text was not written". Errors from starting and waiting read "{program} did not start" and "{program} did not finish". `test_support` has `Copied`, `recording()` and `broken()`. `broken` uses a named fn `refuse` instead of a closure so rustfmt has only one way to format it. Tests: `cat` gives Ok, `false` gives Err, and a missing program's error says it did not start.

conversation.rs: new field `prompts: Vec<usize>`, filled only by `say`. Private helpers are `unfinished_from`, `finished_answer`, `prompt_before` (uses `rfind`) and `text_at`. `text_at` uses `get`, so there is no indexing by number. The public methods are `last_answer` and `last_exchange` ("{prompt}\n\n{answer}"). Six tests cover the cases the planner listed.

Decision: `last_answer` must return `&str`, so it returns the last single Root entry. If a chain report arrives in the middle of root's streaming, the answer is stored as two entries, and only the part after the report is copied. This is rare.

tui/app.rs: `Services.clipboard`, a private `App.clipboard`, and `pub(super) status_note`. `handle` clears the note on its first line. Constants are `COPY_ANSWER_KEY` 'y', `COPY_BLOCK_KEY` 'Y' and `NOTHING_TO_COPY`. Free fn `copy_note` builds the message. `copy_answer` and `copy_block` are wired into `run_command` before the tab-number branch. The test helpers `app_with(dir, crew, clipboard)` and `copying` were changed, and I added `streamed` and `answered`. Six tests: a markdown table is copied exactly with its character count, Y copies "one\n\nfirst", the block before a still-printing answer is copied, an empty chat reports there is nothing to copy, the next key clears the note, and a broken clipboard gives "not copied: no clipboard here".

Decision: the note is cleared on every key event, including releases. crossterm on macOS sends key releases only when keyboard enhancement is on, and ratatui::init() does not turn it on.

tui.rs: `COMMAND_HINT` now includes both keys. It is 88 characters, so it fits the 100-column test screen. `hint(app) -> &str` returns the note if there is one, otherwise `mode_hint(app)`. That is the old chain of hints, split out into its own function. Test: after Ctrl-X y the screen shows "answer copied · characters: 5". After 'a' it shows READING_HINT and no "copied".

session.rs passes `Clipboard::system()`. README: new paragraph about copying blocks. No new dependencies and no comments. Every match is exhaustive, and imports follow rustfmt's 2024 order. Chains near the 60-character limit were formatted by hand to match what rustfmt does.
